headline_marked: 3 sent to jail over [[attack on Salman Muqtadir's studio]]
headline: 3 sent to jail over attack on Salman Muqtadir's studio
summary: Police arrested several suspects after a mob of 50 people stormed the content creator's 'Brown Fish' studio, causing massive damage and looting equipment.
details: Three suspects—Mohammad Mamun, Mohammad Aslam, and Munna—have been sent to jail after a court hearing. Police are seeking a five-day remand for the accused in connection with the attack on content creator Salman Muqtadir's studio.

The incident occurred at the New Guinea Properties Limited project area in West Matikata, Cantonment. Approximately 50 attackers stormed the area, firing about 50 rounds of bullets and using knives, cleavers, and sticks to attack.

During the chaos, the attackers targeted Salman Muqtadir's 'Brown Fish' studio, where they engaged in widespread vandalism and looting. Several people, including site engineer Mohammad Parvez, were seriously injured during the assault.
The attackers looted cash, laptops, computers, cameras, and professional media equipment. The total loss is estimated at 1.42 crore BDT in damages and 1.50 crore BDT in stolen goods.
When Cantonment police arrived at the scene, the attackers fired shots at them. Police responded with five shotgun rounds in self-defense to control the situation.
Two suspects were arrested immediately from the scene, and a third was later apprehended. Police have recovered domestic weapons and bullet casings from the suspects.
caption:
A mob of 50 people stormed Salman Muqtadir's studio, looting over 3 crore BDT in equipment and damages. 3 suspects are now behind bars.

Three suspects—Mohammad Mamun, Mohammad Aslam, and Munna—have been sent to jail after a court hearing. Police are seeking a five-day remand for the accused in connection with the attack on content creator Salman Muqtadir's studio.

The incident occurred at the New Guinea Properties Limited project area in West Matikata, Cantonment. Approximately 50 attackers stormed the area, firing about 50 rounds of bullets and using knives, cleavers, and sticks to attack.

During the chaos, the attackers targeted Salman Muqtadir's 'Brown Fish' studio, where they engaged in widespread vandalism and looting. Several people, including site engineer Mohammad Parvez, were seriously injured during the assault.

The attackers looted cash, laptops, computers, cameras, and professional media equipment. The total loss is estimated at 1.42 crore BDT in damages and 1.50 crore BDT in stolen goods.

When Cantonment police arrived at the scene, the attackers fired shots at them. Police responded with five shotgun rounds in self-defense to control the situation.

Two suspects were arrested immediately from the scene, and a third was later apprehended. Police have recovered domestic weapons and bullet casings from the suspects.

headline_marked: Constitution amendment bill [[likely in January]], referendum proposed
headline: Constitution amendment bill likely in January, referendum proposed
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed says a referendum will be held before the President's signature if the preamble changes.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed announced that a bill to amend the constitution will be introduced in the National Parliament in January.
He stated that if changes are made to the preamble, a referendum will be organized before the President signs the bill into law.
The announcement was made on Sunday during a meeting with editors and leaders of journalist organizations to gather feedback on the constitutional amendments.
The Home Minister emphasized that the process will be driven by national unity rather than division, aiming to implement the 'July Charter'.
He also invited opposition parties to join the discussions to ensure a broad consensus on the constitutional changes.
A 12-member special committee on constitutional amendment was formed on July 13, though opposition parties have so far declined to participate or provide representatives.
caption:
A referendum on the constitution? Bangladesh is planning a major legal overhaul in January.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed announced that a bill to amend the constitution will be introduced in the National Parliament in January.

He stated that if changes are made to the preamble, a referendum will be organized before the President signs the bill into law.

The announcement was made on Sunday during a meeting with editors and leaders of journalist organizations to gather feedback on the constitutional amendments.

The Home Minister emphasized that the process will be driven by national unity rather than division, aiming to implement the 'July Charter'.

He also invited opposition parties to join the discussions to ensure a broad consensus on the constitutional changes.

A 12-member special committee on constitutional amendment was formed on July 13, though opposition parties have so far declined to participate or provide representatives.
